claims.text: Nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution catalysts have enhanced catalytic activity for ethanol oxidation.
Applied potential and reactants induce surface restructuring during ethanol oxidation.
The induced restructuring selectively enriches the catalyst surface in oxidized Ru and forms active Ru–O sites.
Ru–O sites provide more favorable adsorption and activation of ethanol.
Formation of Ru–O sites lowers the energy barrier for ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
The intended initial catalyst is a homogeneous nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid solution with uniformly distributed atoms and minimal pre-existing surface oxide.
A simultaneous controlled increase in electrochemical potential and ethanol concentration is proposed to trigger surface restructuring and Ru-oxide formation.
Increasing applied potential and ethanol concentration causes local Ru segregation followed by Ru oxidation.
The resulting oxidized Ru sites promote subsequent ethanol-oxidation steps and increase overall catalytic activity.
Relative to low ethanol concentration and static potential, the intervention will measurably increase the Ru oxidation state.
The increase in Ru oxidation state will correlate with a higher ethanol-oxidation current density.
The intervention will produce detectable intermediate adsorbates such as acetaldehyde or other partial-oxidation products.
Low ethanol concentration and constant potential constitute the proposed baseline.
The solid-solution structure remains virtually unchanged under the proposed baseline conditions.
The mechanism is expected to hold from approximately 0.7 to 1.0 V versus RHE at ambient to moderate temperatures.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply in either acidic or alkaline electrolytes.
Extreme potentials or temperatures may cause irreversible catalyst changes outside the proposed mechanism.
Operando XAS, ambient-pressure XPS, in situ TEM, and electrochemical current measurements can track oxidation, segregation, morphology, adsorbates, and activity.
The hypothesis is declared falsified only if the intervention produces neither detectable Ru oxidation or segregation nor an increase in ethanol-oxidation current density.
